events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.94)
events.body: This is a driver-side no-show cancellation, so NS-0 routes the case to NS-1/NS-2 [F3][NS-0]. The trace settles element (i) in the driver's favour: an "I'm Here" tap was logged at 22:37:10 [F5][NS-1]. NS-1 therefore turns on whether the tap was made at the pickup point and whether the driver then waited there over three minutes; the system records say no. The driver's closest approach to Woodlands Civic Centre was 868 m at 22:36:25 and he never entered the 200 m radius [F1], and driver_arrived_at is null, i.e. the platform never recorded him at the pickup [F4][NS-1]. At the moment of the tap he was 1000 m away and spent 0 s inside the radius afterwards [F5][NS-1], and his 5 min 5 s stationary period ran 993 m from the pickup, at (1.4449, 103.7876) [F2][NS-1]. NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both fail on those numbers [F1][F2][F5][NS-1]. The driver's chat claim of presence ("I'm here already, silver Toyota Altis, please come out") and his written statement that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited more than three minutes at the pickup [F9][F12] are contradicted by the gps records [F1][F5], and system records override statements [F12][NS-1]. what_would_change: Had NS-1 (ii) held ((ii) within 200 m of pickup AT THE MOMENT of the tap), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.
Had NS-1 (iii) held ((iii) stayed at the pickup > 3 min after the tap, until cancelling), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver never came within 200 m of the Woodlands Civic Centre pickup point during the whole trip: his closest approach was 868 m at 22:36:25, and he then sat stationary 993 m away from 22:36:45 until he cancelled at 22:41:50.

The platform never recorded the driver as arriving at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), and GPS shows he spent 0 seconds inside 200 m after tapping 'I'm Here'; NS-1(ii) therefore fails, so the $6.61 no-show fee cannot stand.

The driver's own statement that he 'pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup' is contradicted by the system records: at the moment of the tap (22:37:10) he was 1000 m from the pickup point, so his no-show basis fails under NS-2.
The $6.61 cancellation fee charged to the rider (F7) must be refunded in full because the driver cancelled on a no-show claim that does not meet the NS-1 conditions.

Because the driver tapped 'I'm Here' while GPS placed him far outside the pickup point (1000 m at the tap, never within 200 m), this is an abuse of the arrival/cancellation button warranting a separate account-review flag alongside the refund.
The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days, consistent with a repeated pattern of no-show fee claims rather than an isolated error, which supports sending his account for review.

weaknesses: The driver did wait in one place for 5 min 5 s (F2) and messaged the rider twice (F9 'I'm here already, please come out'; F11 'Waited more than 3 min, cancelling'), so the other side will argue he made a genuine attempt to collect the rider and that the rider's own chat reply at 22:38 (F10) does not prove the rider was actually at the pickup point.

The rider's account is supported only by chat (F10), and the case file contains no GPS or geofence record confirming the rider was at the pickup point, so the driver may argue the rider was also not there; however this does not cure the driver's own failure to be within range (F1, F5).
The driver's stationarity at 993 m (F2) lasted longer than 3 minutes, so the other side may argue the spirit of NS-1(iii) is met even though NS-1(ii) plainly is not (F1, F5).

claims.assertion: The platform's own GPS record shows the driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 868 m and he never came within 200 m (F1), and driver_arrived_at is null (F4).
At the moment the 'I'm Here' tap was logged (22:37:10) the driver was 1000 m from the pickup point and spent 0 s inside the 200 m radius afterwards, so requirement NS-1(ii) is not met (F5).
Any stationary waiting by the driver took place 993 m away from the pickup point from 22:36:45 to 22:41:50 (F2), which is not waiting 'at the pick-up point' within the meaning of NS-1(iii).

The driver's chat message 'I'm here already, silver Toyota Altis, please come out' (F9) and his written statement that he waited at the pickup (F12) are contradicted by the GPS record (F1, F5), and the system records prevail, so the $6.61 no-show fee cannot stand on those statements.

The rider was present and actively trying to locate the driver, asking at 22:38 'I'm at the pickup point and I don't see any car. Where are you?' (F10), consistent with the driver never having been at the pickup (F1).

The conditions for a $6.61 no-show cancellation fee under NS-1 are not cumulatively satisfied and therefore, per NS-2, the fee must be refunded in full — the amount is evidenced by the fare record of $6.61 (F7).

The record also shows a contradiction between the tap event (F5) and the timeline entry that driver_pressed_here_at is null (F6); in either reading the driver was not within 200 m of the pickup, so NS-1(ii) still fails.

The driver's 90-day history shows 2 prior no-show disputes, both upheld (F17), which on the face of the record supports the rider's account that the arrival/waiting-button process was misused rather than being an isolated GPS error.

The driver cancelled 8 min 50 s after acceptance while located ~993 m from the pickup (F2, F3), so there is no traffic justification in the record: no speed-band data and no incidents on the route during the trip window (F13, F14).

weaknesses: The driver did press a button logged at 22:37:10 and sent a message at 22:37 claiming to be present (F5, F9); a judge could read the driver-side intent sympathetically even though the GPS shows he was 1000 m away (F1, F5).
The driver is a long-tenured, high-rated account (2071 days, 4.84 rating, 1152 trips in 90 d) (F17), which may invite leniency and cut against an account flag.
Light rain (1.8 mm) at the time (F15) may be argued by the driver as an excuse for stopping short of the pickup, though it does not satisfy NS-1(ii)/(iii).
The rider has 355 days of account history and 1 dispute in 90 days, 0 upheld (F16), which is neutral rather than supportive and gives the judge no rider-side misconduct to weigh against the driver.
The discrepancy between F5 (a tap was logged) and F6 (no tap recorded) could be attacked by the other side as data inconsistency, though neither version puts the driver inside 200 m (F1).

points.response: Agreed on the substance: the GPS record (closest approach 868 m, never within 200 m, F1) and the null driver_arrived_at (F4) mean NS-1(ii) fails, and the driver himself does not contest it.
Conceded — F5 shows the tap at 22:37:10 occurred 1000 m from the pickup with 0 s inside the radius, so NS-1(ii) is plainly unsatisfied and NS-2 requires a full refund.
Conceded — the 5 min 5 s stationary period at 993 m (F2) is not waiting 'at the pick-up point', so NS-1(iii) also fails on the correct location test.
Conceded: the chat claim of presence (F9) and the driver's statement (F12) lose to the GPS records (F1, F5) under the system-records-prevail rule, so no finding can rest on the statements alone.

Conceded as far as it goes: the rider's 22:38 message asking where the car was (F10) is consistent with the GPS showing the driver 868 m away at best (F1), and it supplies no independent proof of the driver's position.
Conceded in full: NS-1's cumulative conditions fail, so NS-2 grants the rider a full refund of the $6.61 recorded in the fare table (F7, F3), payable as a Ryde voucher under NS-7.

Accepted with one rider-side addition: whether the tap is read from F5 or F6, the driver was never inside 200 m (F1), so either reading fails NS-1(ii); the rider separately asks the account flag on the F5 reading, where a here-button was pressed 1000 m away.

Supported and relied on, but only as a supporting flag ground: the driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17) corroborate a repeated pattern, and under NS-2/RD-6 profile facts may back the flag_account action, never the finding itself, which rests on F1/F4/F5.

Conceded — the cancellation came 8 min 50 s after acceptance with the driver ~993 m from pickup (F3, F2), and the traffic record shows no speed bands and no incidents on the route (F13, F14), so no justified-reroute excuse exists; light rain (F15) explains nothing about stopping 1 km short.

Concede: the GPS record is what it is — the driver's closest approach was 868 m and he never entered the 200 m radius, and he was stationary 993 m from the pickup when he cancelled (F1, F2); under NS-1(ii) that segment cannot be defended.

Concede the NS-1(ii) element: driver_arrived_at is null and the driver spent 0 s inside 200 m after the 22:37:10 tap (F4, F5), so no-show fee liability under NS-1 is not established — but this is a billing defect in the app workflow, not proof of dishonest intent by the driver.

Partially concede: the statement in F12 loses to the GPS record (F5, F1) as the rules require, so the fee falls; but the driver did in fact stop and wait for over three minutes and messaged the rider twice (F2, F9, F11), which shows a genuine attempt to collect the rider rather than a fabricated attempt to collect a fee.

The refund follows from the failed NS-1 conditions and the $6.61 fare record (F7), and I do not resist it; however NS-7 governs its form, so it must be issued as a voucher rather than cash, and it should not be accompanied by a fraud flag where the record shows no voluntary misconduct.

This is where the rider overreaches: the record shows contradictory entries — a tap logged at 22:37:10 (F5) while the timeline records driver_pressed_here_at as null (F6) — which points to a technical/geofence error, not deliberate abuse of the button, and no other indicator of fraud appears in the record.

The profile fact F17 may only ever be an additional action and can never decide the case (NS-6/RD-6 logic), and the rider's own side of the table shows 1 dispute in 90 days with 0 upheld (F16): neither profile establishes a mala fide pattern in the GPS data here (F1, F2).
